luca-a-roma-35:s18: So many people. I had not seen this in a long time.
luca-a-roma-35:s19: They are neighborhood people. They wanted a reason to come.
luca-a-roma-35:s20: A woman said she liked the coffee, and that she would come back the next week.
luca-a-roma-35:s21: Luca brought water to a table and listened to people talk about Rome and work.
luca-a-roma-35:s22: He did not understand all the words, but he understood the important thing: the room was alive.
luca-a-roma-35:s23: You are good at the door. People see you and come in.
luca-a-roma-35:s24: Thanks. Today I work here with you, not alone.
luca-a-roma-35:s25: The owner served two coffees and looked at the room again.
luca-a-roma-35:s26: It works, at least today. I don’t know about Monday.
luca-a-roma-35:s27: Today counts. The people are here now.
luca-a-roma-35:s28: Some customers asked if there was a celebration the next week too.
luca-a-roma-35:s29: Not every Saturday. But the café is open. You can come back.
luca-a-roma-35:s30: Marco brought bread to Nonna Rosa and listened to the voices near the tables.
luca-a-roma-35:s31: When a family came in late, Luca found a place near the window.
luca-a-roma-35:s32: The music stayed not too loud. People stayed to talk.
luca-a-roma-35:s33: Giulia looked at Luca and made a small sign: it was going well.
luca-a-roma-35:s34: The owner did not make big speeches. He only worked and watched.
luca-a-roma-35:s35: The problem was not finished yet. It was only a full afternoon.
luca-a-roma-35:s36: But after weeks of empty tables, today there were customers and friends together.
luca-a-roma-35:s37: Nonna Rosa called Luca and told him to stay near the door.
luca-a-roma-35:s38: People come in if they see someone. You stay there.
luca-a-roma-35:s40: Sofia put the phone on the table. Now the phone was no longer needed.
luca-a-roma-35:s41: The small celebration was working, at least for these hours.
luca-a-roma-35:s42: Luca felt less fear, but he did not say that the problem was finished.
luca-a-roma-35:s43: The owner was seeing customers. That was more important than words.
luca-a-roma-35:s44: Toward evening some people left, and some people stayed longer.
luca-a-roma-35:s45: Now Luca knew one thing: people could come back.
luca-a-roma-35:s46: He still had to ask for the rest. Not today, but soon.
luca-a-roma-36:s01: Later, when the room was full, Giulia made a sign to Luca.
luca-a-roma-36:s02: Speak. Two words. People are here also for this place.
luca-a-roma-36:s03: Me? I don’t know. I am afraid.
luca-a-roma-36:s04: We can handle it, if you want. But it seems to me that you can.
luca-a-roma-36:s05: Luca looked at Nonna Rosa. She smiled and said: “It’s fine like this.”
luca-a-roma-36:s06: Then Luca stopped in the room, near the full tables.
luca-a-roma-36:s07: Good evening. I work here. A few months ago I arrived in Rome, alone.
luca-a-roma-36:s08: Now I have a home, a job, and friends. This café is a part of all this.
luca-a-roma-36:s09: If you like it, come back. Not only today. Also Monday, also Thursday.
luca-a-roma-36:s10: We need people on the days of the week. Not only for a celebration.
luca-a-roma-36:s11: Some people smiled. Some people said “good” quietly.
luca-a-roma-36:s12: The owner listened near the kitchen, without speaking.
luca-a-roma-36:s13: Marco brought a coffee to Nonna Rosa, and she listened to Luca well.
luca-a-roma-36:s14: After the words, the celebration continued. The music was not too loud. People stayed.
luca-a-roma-36:s15: You said little, and you said a lot. All right.
luca-a-roma-36:s16: The owner listened to you. I saw it.
luca-a-roma-36:s17: All right. I only wanted to say one true thing.
luca-a-roma-36:s18: A family asked about the week’s hours. Giulia explained, glad to do more.
luca-a-roma-36:s19: Sofia was near Luca, not like a person who helps a new guy, but like a friend.
luca-a-roma-36:s20: You asked for the right thing. Coming back, not only staying here one day.
luca-a-roma-36:s21: Yes. If they come back, the owner sees work. If not, a nice day remains.
luca-a-roma-36:s22: When the light changed, some people left, and some people stayed longer.
luca-a-roma-36:s23: The owner called Luca near the kitchen, in a not-loud voice.
luca-a-roma-36:s24: Today the café worked. I saw the tables. I saw the people.
luca-a-roma-36:s25: I still don’t know everything. But today yes. You asked well.
luca-a-roma-36:s26: Thank you for saying yes to this celebration.
luca-a-roma-36:s27: You did the work. I only opened the kitchen.
luca-a-roma-36:s28: Luca listened. The owner was not talking about the future. He was talking about today.
luca-a-roma-36:s30: Her too. Tomorrow we talk about hours and work. Not now.
luca-a-roma-36:s31: Giulia heard and made a small sign to Luca: later.
luca-a-roma-36:s32: Sofia told Luca to drink water and to stay still a moment.
luca-a-roma-36:s33: You spoke clearly. Now let’s let the room work.
luca-a-roma-36:s34: Marco washed the plates and said little, as always.
luca-a-roma-36:s35: People stay. This helps more than many words.
luca-a-roma-36:s37: Nonna Rosa paid for the coffee and said she would come back Thursday, if she could.
luca-a-roma-36:s38: The owner heard that and looked at the bill again.
luca-a-roma-36:s39: Come back. We work. We see the week.
luca-a-roma-36:s40: Sofia smiled, truly, not like a person who explains everything.
luca-a-roma-36:s41: When the celebration was smaller, the owner turned the music down a little.
luca-a-roma-36:s42: Today is enough. Tomorrow is Monday. We work.
luca-a-roma-36:s43: Luca helped put the plates in the kitchen and thought about Giulia’s hours.
luca-a-roma-36:s44: The owner’s yes was not yet on the future. It was on the day.
luca-a-roma-36:s45: Tomorrow we hear the owner. Today we did enough.
luca-a-roma-36:s46: Yes. Today people arrived. Tomorrow we ask for the rest.
luca-a-roma-36:s47: Sofia looked at the still-full room and spoke quietly.
luca-a-roma-36:s48: Today counts. Tomorrow we see the hours.
luca-a-roma-37:s01: Monday morning Luca went to work with a little fear.
luca-a-roma-37:s02: A celebration is one day. Monday is the life of every week.
luca-a-roma-37:s03: When he opened the door, there were already two customers at a table.
luca-a-roma-37:s04: It was not a full room, but it was not empty like the week before.
luca-a-roma-37:s05: Good morning. See? Someone came back.
luca-a-roma-37:s06: Yes. It seems to me a first real day, even if small.
luca-a-roma-37:s07: They worked. The coffee, the water, the bills. Everyday things, but different.
luca-a-roma-37:s08: In the afternoon the owner asked Luca and Giulia to stay a moment.
luca-a-roma-37:s09: I’m not selling. Not now. The café stays. At least this month, and the next.
luca-a-roma-37:s10: Thank you. For me it is important to stay.
luca-a-roma-37:s11: You two work more, if you want. I need hours, not a new person.
luca-a-roma-37:s12: Luca heard the words “if you want” and understood that he could choose.
luca-a-roma-37:s13: Yes. I accept. I need the pay, and I like this place.
luca-a-roma-37:s14: I accept too. But I also want to organize, not only serve.
luca-a-roma-37:s15: All right. We’ll see. You make a weekly plan. I listen.
luca-a-roma-37:s16: Giulia smiled, at last, like a person who was heard.
luca-a-roma-37:s17: For Luca it was good news twice: the job stayed, and Giulia had her place.
luca-a-roma-37:s18: The big problem was not completely finished. A month is not a future.
luca-a-roma-37:s19: But today they could work without that fear from yesterday.
luca-a-roma-37:s21: A few more hours every week. Then we look at the customers.
luca-a-roma-37:s22: If people stay, I give more hours. If not, we change.
luca-a-roma-37:s23: Clear. It is not forever. It is for now.
luca-a-roma-37:s25: In the evening Luca counted the money. This month’s rent was safer.
luca-a-roma-37:s26: He wrote a message to Sofia and Marco: the café stays, for now.
luca-a-roma-37:s27: Sofia answered right away. Marco answered later, glad, and he is still looking for a job.
luca-a-roma-37:s28: Luca closed the window and thought about the new hours.
luca-a-roma-37:s29: More hours meant more money, and also less free time.
luca-a-roma-37:s30: He had to talk about this with Sofia. It was not something to decide alone.
luca-a-roma-37:s31: Giulia called Luca before leaving and talked about the weekly plan.
luca-a-roma-37:s32: I prepare a clear schedule. You watch the door and the customers.
luca-a-roma-37:s33: All right. And if customers don’t come back?
luca-a-roma-37:s34: Then the owner changes again. But today we have real hours.
luca-a-roma-37:s35: Luca listened. The news was good, and it was not closed.
luca-a-roma-37:s36: The café was not sold. The work was not finished. The future was not closed.
luca-a-roma-37:s37: But for the first time after so many weeks, Luca could pay and stay.
luca-a-roma-37:s38: He thought of Marco, still looking for work, and of Sofia, with her full days.
luca-a-roma-37:s39: Tomorrow, or later, he had to see Sofia. He wanted to talk about the new hours.
luca-a-roma-37:s40: It was not closed news. It was a clearer month of work.
luca-a-roma-37:s41: When Luca went home, he thought again of Saturday and the full tables.
luca-a-roma-37:s42: That day had given the owner a reason not to sell the café.
luca-a-roma-37:s43: He put the phone near the window and read Sofia’s message again.
luca-a-roma-37:s44: Good. Let’s talk soon about the hours.
luca-a-roma-37:s45: Yes. I accept more, but I don’t want to be left without time for friends.
luca-a-roma-37:s46: He did not have to answer everything in one evening. He only had to leave the question open.
luca-a-roma-37:s47: The café stayed. Now there were more hours. Life still asked him to choose.
luca-a-roma-37:s48: For this evening, that was enough.
luca-a-roma-34:s03:extended: When he opened the door, Giulia was already in the room, with the tables open and ready.
luca-a-roma-34:s18:extended: They put out the plates, the water, and the coffee near the tables. Luca washed the tables twice.
luca-a-roma-35:s04:extended: Wait a moment. It is early. Neighborhood people eat and then go out.
luca-a-roma-35:s20:extended: A woman said she liked the coffee, and that she would come back the next week, for sure.
luca-a-roma-36:s09:extended: If you like it, come back here. Not only today. Also Monday, also Thursday.
luca-a-roma-36:s24:extended: Today the café worked well. I saw the tables. I saw the people.
luca-a-roma-37:s12:extended: Luca heard the words "if you want" and understood that he could choose the hours.
luca-a-roma-37:s14:extended: I accept too. But I also want to organize the week, not only serve.
luca-a-roma-38:s01: Two evenings later, Luca and Sofia met for a dinner in the center.
luca-a-roma-38:s02: The place was small and quiet, with little light and few tables.
luca-a-roma-38:s03: Sofia arrived a little late, because work had been long.
luca-a-roma-38:s04: So. The café is staying. Are you happy about the new hours?
luca-a-roma-38:s05: Yes. I have more money. This month’s rent is safer.
luca-a-roma-38:s06: But I also have less time. The week is already full.
luca-a-roma-38:s07: Luca took the water. Sofia listened, and she did not decide for him.
luca-a-roma-38:s08: What do you want, really? Not what the owner said.
luca-a-roma-38:s09: I want to stay in Rome. I want to work. But I don’t want only work.
luca-a-roma-38:s10: I want time for friends and for home.
luca-a-roma-38:s11: That is clear. Then the hours must not take the whole week.
luca-a-roma-38:s12: While they talked, the room was quiet.
luca-a-roma-38:s13: They ate pasta and talked about Sofia’s work.
luca-a-roma-38:s14: My work is a lot. Some evenings I am tired. Some evenings I am fine.
luca-a-roma-38:s15: Me too. After Saturday, the new hours feel big.
luca-a-roma-38:s16: If you accept all the hours, when do you see your friends?
luca-a-roma-38:s17: I don’t know. Maybe I see friends little. And I don’t like that.
luca-a-roma-38:s18: Then it isn’t a yes-or-no question. It’s a schedule question.
luca-a-roma-38:s19: Luca thought about the rent, then about friends, then about Giulia.
luca-a-roma-38:s20: Giulia makes the week’s plan. I can ask for a clear schedule.
luca-a-roma-38:s21: Yes. Talk to the owner about what you need. He listens.
luca-a-roma-38:s22: When Sofia said “what you need,” Luca understood the important thing.
luca-a-roma-38:s23: He didn’t have to be afraid to ask. He only had to be clear.
luca-a-roma-38:s24: You want more hours, but not all of them. That’s fine.
luca-a-roma-38:s25: They talked about real days, not about a long year.
luca-a-roma-38:s26: Monday and Wednesday evenings, I want to stay free.
luca-a-roma-38:s27: Tuesday and Thursday I can work more, if the owner wants.
luca-a-roma-38:s28: Saturday and Sunday are hard, because the café needs people.
luca-a-roma-38:s29: That seems like a plan to me. It isn’t big, but it’s a start.
luca-a-roma-38:s30: Sofia didn’t say many words. She asked questions, and she listened.
luca-a-roma-38:s31: For me you are a friend, not only the person from the first days.
luca-a-roma-38:s32: I know. Now we talk because we want to, not because you are new.
luca-a-roma-38:s33: Luca smiled. The dinner was small. Every word was clear.
luca-a-roma-38:s34: Tomorrow I talk with the owner. I ask for more hours, but not all.
luca-a-roma-38:s35: Good. And if the owner says no to the hours?
luca-a-roma-38:s36: Then I look for another way. But first I ask.
luca-a-roma-38:s37: After dinner they walked a little toward the neighborhood.
luca-a-roma-38:s38: Rome in the evening was full of people, and they talked quietly.
luca-a-roma-38:s39: They didn’t decide the long future. They decided the next day.
luca-a-roma-38:s40: See you soon. Don’t stay only among the café hours.
luca-a-roma-38:s41: I won’t stay only that way. Monday and Wednesday evenings are free.
luca-a-roma-38:s42: Sofia made a yes sign, happy in a quiet way.
luca-a-roma-38:s43: When Luca got home, he wrote two words on the phone.
luca-a-roma-38:s44: Tomorrow: a clear schedule with the owner. More hours, not all.
luca-a-roma-38:s45: He put the phone near the window and waited a moment.
luca-a-roma-38:s46: The café was staying. The new hours were staying. Now there was also a plan.
luca-a-roma-38:s47: It was a small, clear thing for the new week.
luca-a-roma-38:s48: Tomorrow he had to talk. Tonight, this was enough.
luca-a-roma-38:s49: He thought about Marco, still looking for work, and about Giulia with her plan.
luca-a-roma-38:s50: Then he turned off the light. Tomorrow started with a clear question.
luca-a-roma-38:s09:extended: I want to stay in Rome and I want to work. But I don’t want only work every day.
luca-a-roma-38:s26:extended: Monday and Wednesday evenings, I want to stay free for friends.
luca-a-roma-39:s01: The next day Luca talked with the owner, as decided with Sofia.
luca-a-roma-39:s02: I want more hours, but not all. Monday and Wednesday evenings I want free time.
luca-a-roma-39:s03: Tuesday and Thursday I can do more. Saturday and Sunday, as needed.
luca-a-roma-39:s04: Okay. You’re clear. Let’s make a fair schedule with Giulia.
luca-a-roma-39:s05: Giulia listened from the door and took paper for the plan.
luca-a-roma-39:s06: Good. That way I know who is in the room, and when. I don’t change every day.
luca-a-roma-39:s07: While they were making the schedule, Marco arrived at the café door.
luca-a-roma-39:s08: Sorry. Can I talk a moment? I need to tell you something.
luca-a-roma-39:s09: The owner motioned yes. Luca put the plates on the table.
luca-a-roma-39:s10: I’m looking for work. I haven’t found a big place. But I can help here.
luca-a-roma-39:s11: On busy days. Few hours. I’m not asking for a job forever.
luca-a-roma-39:s12: Luca looked at Giulia. She looked at the owner, then she spoke.
luca-a-roma-39:s13: On busy days we need one more person. We’ve seen that.
luca-a-roma-39:s14: Few hours. Little money. It isn’t a big job. If you want, we’ll try.
luca-a-roma-39:s15: I want to. Thanks. For me it’s already a start.
luca-a-roma-39:s16: Marco motioned yes, and nothing more.
luca-a-roma-39:s17: If you work here, we see each other more. That’s fine for me.
luca-a-roma-39:s18: For me too. Friends and a bit of money. Better than nothing.
luca-a-roma-39:s19: Luca was happy in a quiet way. Marco’s problem remained.
luca-a-roma-39:s20: But there was a real first day at the café, with the people of the place.
luca-a-roma-39:s21: In the afternoon Sofia stopped by, because she wanted to hear the news.
luca-a-roma-39:s22: Marco helps on busy days. It isn’t much, but it’s a place.
luca-a-roma-39:s23: Good. You’re not only looking alone anymore. You have something real.
luca-a-roma-39:s24: Marco said little. Yes. Thanks. Then he looked at Giulia’s schedule.
luca-a-roma-39:s25: Giulia showed the days: a full Saturday, and some evenings in the week.
luca-a-roma-39:s26: You come when the room is full. I organize. Luca has his hours.
luca-a-roma-39:s27: Clear. I do what is needed, and nothing more.
luca-a-roma-39:s29: We’ll try two weeks. Then we look at the customers and the money.
luca-a-roma-39:s30: Nobody said the café was safe forever. But today it was working better.
luca-a-roma-39:s31: Luca saw the new hours on his schedule: more work, but not everything.
luca-a-roma-39:s32: Monday and Wednesday evenings stayed free, as he had told Sofia.
luca-a-roma-39:s33: Sofia stayed a little, because she wanted to be there.
luca-a-roma-39:s34: I’m here because I want to be. Not only because Luca has a problem.
luca-a-roma-39:s35: I know. And I like that.
luca-a-roma-39:s36: Marco took a little water and asked about Saturday’s schedule.
luca-a-roma-39:s37: In the evening the four of them ate near the café, with bread and something to drink.
luca-a-roma-39:s38: It was a dinner after a long day.
luca-a-roma-39:s39: The café is staying. Marco helps. Luca has a clear schedule. I organize.
luca-a-roma-39:s40: I’m here too because I choose to be.
luca-a-roma-39:s42: To Rome, then. And to this small job.
luca-a-roma-39:s43: Luca listened. The group’s life seemed safer, but not closed.
luca-a-roma-39:s44: When he got home, he saw a message from his mother on the phone.
luca-a-roma-39:s45: I’ll call you tomorrow. I have a job proposal. It isn’t in Rome.
luca-a-roma-39:s46: Luca read the words twice. He didn’t answer right away.
luca-a-roma-39:s47: He put the phone on the table and looked at Giulia’s schedule, already ready.
luca-a-roma-39:s48: Tomorrow there was the call. Today there was a place for Marco.
luca-a-roma-39:s50: Before sleeping he wrote to Sofia: Tomorrow Mom talks. I’ll tell you after.
luca-a-roma-39:s51: Then he turned off the light. The café was staying. The future, still open.
luca-a-roma-39:s02:extended: I want more hours, but not all. Monday and Wednesday evenings I want free time for home and friends.
luca-a-roma-39:s14:extended: Few hours. Little money. It isn’t a big job. If you want, we’ll try two weeks.
luca-a-roma-40:s01: The next day, in the afternoon, Mom called Luca at home.
luca-a-roma-40:s02: Luca took the phone and listened carefully.
luca-a-roma-40:s03: Mom said: there is a place in a bar near home.
luca-a-roma-40:s04: A family friend is looking for someone. The job is for two months.
luca-a-roma-40:s05: It starts next month. There is more money than now.
luca-a-roma-40:s06: You have to answer this week. If you say yes, you leave Rome for a while.
luca-a-roma-40:s08: A real job, in another city, near the family, for two months.
luca-a-roma-40:s09: He told his mother: I understand. I need to think. I’ll answer you soon.
luca-a-roma-40:s10: After the call he sat down. He looked at the street outside the window.
luca-a-roma-40:s11: He thought about the café, the new schedule, Giulia, Marco, Sofia.
luca-a-roma-40:s12: In Rome he had a home, a job, and friends. It wasn’t the first day anymore.
luca-a-roma-40:s13: The proposal was good. He had to choose, not leave Rome out of fear.
luca-a-roma-40:s14: He put the phone on the table and took Giulia’s schedule.
luca-a-roma-40:s15: Monday and Wednesday evenings were free. The other days he worked more.
luca-a-roma-40:s16: Marco came on busy days. The café had more customers than before, enough.
luca-a-roma-40:s17: If he left, he left these things. If he stayed, he said no to money and to home.
luca-a-roma-40:s18: He wasn’t afraid of the proposal. He needed to choose well.
luca-a-roma-40:s19: He walked a little, then he decided.
luca-a-roma-40:s20: For now I stay in Rome. This work, this home, these people.
luca-a-roma-40:s21: He called his mother again and spoke quietly, but clearly.
luca-a-roma-40:s22: Thanks. The proposal is good. But for now I stay here. I’m not leaving.
luca-a-roma-40:s23: Mom listened. She wasn’t fully happy, but she understood.
luca-a-roma-40:s24: Okay. If one day you want to leave, you tell me. The place stays open.
luca-a-roma-40:s25: Luca said thanks one more time, and ended the call.
luca-a-roma-40:s26: In the evening, after work, he talked with Giulia while she closed the tables.
luca-a-roma-40:s27: Mom had a proposal: a bar near home, two months, more money.
luca-a-roma-40:s28: I said no. For now I stay. The schedule here works for me.
luca-a-roma-40:s29: Clear. You chose. Tomorrow the café opens the same.
luca-a-roma-40:s30: Sofia and Marco arrived a little later, because Luca had written a message.
luca-a-roma-40:s31: There was a job proposal outside Rome. I decided to stay, for now.
luca-a-roma-40:s32: Good. Not because it’s easy. Because you want this life here.
luca-a-roma-40:s33: You’re right. It isn’t forever. It’s for now.
luca-a-roma-40:s34: Marco looked at Luca and made a small yes sign.
luca-a-roma-40:s35: Okay. Then see you at work. I’m there on Saturday.
luca-a-roma-40:s37: Tomorrow we open in the morning. The schedule is ready. Nothing special.
luca-a-roma-40:s38: They didn’t throw a party. They talked a little, then they went home.
luca-a-roma-40:s40: When Luca got home, he put the phone on the table.
luca-a-roma-40:s41: The proposal remained real. He had said no for now, not forever.
luca-a-roma-40:s42: He prepared things for the morning and looked at the schedule once more.
luca-a-roma-40:s43: The next day he opened the café with Giulia, like every work morning.
luca-a-roma-40:s44: Marco wasn’t there, because it wasn’t a busy day. The room was small, as always.
luca-a-roma-40:s45: Two customers came in. Luca brought coffee and water, as always.
luca-a-roma-40:s47: Today we work. Tomorrow too. This is the job, for now.
